Name: Anonymized Feedback Summary
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST supply an anonymized and desensitized summary of the feedback, questions, and answers about each Ongoing Certification Report as an addendum to the Ongoing Certification Report OR in the next Ongoing Certification Report.

Name: Report Availability
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST supply an Ongoing Certification Report to all necessary parties every 3 months, covering the entire period since the previous summary, in a consistent format that is human readable; this report MUST include high-level summaries of at least the following information:

Name: Feedback Mechanism
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST supply an asynchronous mechanism for all necessary parties to provide feedback or ask questions about each Ongoing Certification Report.

Name: Limit Sensitive Information
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST NOT irresponsibly disclose sensitive information in an Ongoing Certification Report that would likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.

Name: Next Report Date
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST supply the target date for their next Ongoing Certification Report with other public FedRAMP Certification Data.

Name: Responsible Public Certification Report Sharing
Requirement (Class C): Providers MAY responsibly supply some or all of the information an Ongoing Certification Report to the public or other parties if the provider determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.

Name: Spread Out Reports
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD establish a regular 3 month cycle for Ongoing Certification Reports that is spread out from the beginning, middle, or end of each quarter.

Name: Additional Content
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD supply additional information in Quarterly Reviews that the provider determines is of interest, use, or otherwise relevant to agencies.

Name: Quarterly Review Meeting
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications MUST host a synchronous Quarterly Review every 3 months, open to all necessary parties, to review aspects of the most recent Ongoing Certification Reports that the provider determines are of the most relevance to agencies.

Name: No Irresponsible Disclosure
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST NOT irresponsibly disclose sensitive information in a Quarterly Review that would likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.

Name: Next Review Date
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST publicly supply the target date for their next Quarterly Review with other public FedRAMP Certification Data.

Name: Meeting Registration Info
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST supply either a registration link or a downloadable calendar file with meeting information for Quarterly Reviews to all necessary parties.

Name: Restrict Third Parties
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD NOT invite third parties to attend Quarterly Reviews intended for agencies unless they have specific relevance.

Name: Record/Transcribe Reviews
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD record or transcribe Quarterly Reviews and supply them to all necessary parties.

Name: Schedule Around Reports
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD regularly schedule Quarterly Reviews to occur at least 3 business days after releasing an Ongoing Certification Report AND within 10 business days of such release.

Name: Share Content Responsibly
Requirement (Class C): Providers MAY responsibly supply content prepared for a Quarterly Review to the public or other parties if the provider determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.

Name: Share Recordings Responsibly
Requirement (Class C): Providers MAY responsibly supply recordings or transcriptions of Quarterly Reviews to the public or other parties ONLY if the provider removes all agency information (comments, questions, names, etc.) AND determines doing so will NOT likely have an adverse effect on the cloud service offering.

Name: Automated Incident Reporting
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD use automation to minimize human intervention in the process of reporting FedRAMP Reportable Incidents to all affected parties.

Name: Default PAIN Rating
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST treat FedRAMP Reportable Incidents as if they have a Potential Agency Impact N-rating (PAIN) of 5 UNLESS they promptly estimate the PAIN rating following the rule in IEC-CSO-EFI (Estimate Federal Impact).

Name: Estimate Federal Impact
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD promptly estimate the likely adverse impact of an incident on agency customers to assign a Potential Agency Impact N-rating; this step is called Incident Rating.

Name: Evaluate FedRAMP Reportability
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST promptly evaluate incidents to determine if they affect confidentiality or integrity of federal customer data or are likely to affect confidentiality or integrity of federal customer data; such incidents are FedRAMP Reportable Incidents and must be reported following the FedRAMP Incident Evaluation and Communication rules.

Name: Final Incident Report
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications MUST responsibly notify all affected parties by providing a Final Incident Report once the incident has been resolved and recovery is complete, including final updates to all previously reported information.

Name: Initial Incident Report
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications MUST responsibly notify all affected parties after identifying FedRAMP Reportable Incidents by providing an Initial Incident Report with as much of the following information that is available at the time of reporting and/or the current relevant status for each item:

Name: Ongoing Incident Reports
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications MUST responsibly notify all affected parties of ongoing activity as new information becomes available during incident response for FedRAMP Reportable Incidents, including updates (or lack of updates) to all previously reported information and as much of the the following additional information that is available and/or the current relevant status for each item:

Name: Automate Detection
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD use automated services to improve and streamline vulnerability detection and response.
Current Process: Scheduled Nessus scans; PowerShell KEV automation
Gap: Detection partly automated; the detect-to-evaluate handoff is manual
Required Change: Automate the enrichment stage that turns a detection into an evaluated finding (IRV/LEV/PAIN)

Name: Avoid KEVs
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD NOT deploy or otherwise activate new machine-based information resources with Known Exploited Vulnerabilities.
Gap: KEV handling is detect-after-the-fact; no pre-deployment gate to avoid introducing KEVs
Required Change: Add a pre-deploy / golden-image KEV avoidance check so known KEVs are not shipped

Name: Detect After Changes
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD automatically perform vulnerability detection on representative samples of new or significantly changed information resources.
Gap: Scans not reliably triggered by environment change
Required Change: Trigger detection on change events (deploy/config drift), not only on a fixed schedule

Name: Vulnerability Detection
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST systematically, persistently, and promptly discover and identify vulnerabilities within their cloud service offering using appropriate techniques such as assessment, scanning, threat intelligence, vulnerability disclosure mechanisms, bug bounties, penetration testing, incident response, automated control testing, supply chain monitoring, and other relevant capabilities; this process is called vulnerability detection. Vulnerability detection includes persistently verifying and validating that information resources and processes are operating as intended and documented for FedRAMP Practices.
Current Process: Monthly authenticated scans plus daily KEV scan
Gap: Detection exists but not at the Class C per-resource cadence/coverage required by PSD/PDD/PCD
Required Change: Ensure detection covers all in-boundary resources at Class C cadence (3/14/monthly per resource type)

Name: Design For Resilience
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD make design and architecture decisions for their cloud service offering that mitigate the risk of vulnerabilities by default AND decrease the risk and complexity of vulnerability detection and response.
Current Process: Network segmentation and Azure architecture in place
Gap: Resilience that limits single-vulnerability blast radius is not formally documented
Required Change: Document resilience/segmentation that reduces blast radius; feeds the PAIN estimate

Name: Failures Are Vulnerabilities
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST treat problems or failures with their vulnerability detection and response processes as vulnerabilities.
Gap: Detection/telemetry coverage gaps (e.g. hosts outside telemetry, agent gaps) not treated as vulnerabilities
Required Change: Treat detection and telemetry coverage failures as vulnerabilities in the register and Jira

Name: Maintain Security
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD NOT weaken the security of information resources to facilitate vulnerability scanning, detection, or assessment activities.
Gap: No explicit guard against changes that regress security posture
Required Change: Add a change-management check that flags posture-reducing changes

Name: Vulnerability Response
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST systematically, persistently, and promptly track, evaluate, monitor, mitigate, remediate, assess exploitation of, report, and otherwise manage all detected vulnerabilities within their cloud service offering; this process is called vulnerability response.
Current Process: Remediate on CVSS-based SLA from discovery
Gap: Response prioritized by CVSS, not by PAIN x reachability x exploitability
Required Change: Drive response off the Class C PVR matrix (PAIN/IRV/LEV) measured from evaluation date

Name: Sampling
Requirement (Class C): Providers MAY sample effectively identical information resources, especially machine-based information resources, when performing vulnerability detection UNLESS doing so would decrease the efficiency or effectiveness of vulnerability detection.
Gap: No defined representative sample sets
Required Change: Optional: define representative sample sets of similar machine resources (supports PSD)

Name: Remediate KEVs
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD remediate Known Exploited Vulnerabilities according to the due dates in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog (even if the vulnerability has been fully mitigated) as required by CISA Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04 or any successor guidance from CISA.
Current Process: Daily KEV scan, Nessus to Jira to SMTP
Gap: KEV due-date tracking references BOD 22-01 timelines, not BOD 26-04
Required Change: Align KEV due dates to the BOD 26-04 catalog; remediate by due date even if already mitigated

Name: Persistent Machine Verification and Validation for Rev5
Requirement (Class C): Providers of FedRAMP Rev5 Class C offerings MUST verify and validate the status of machine-based information resources at least once every month.
Gap: No persistent automated machine verification/validation as the Rev5 rule expects
Required Change: Stand up persistent automated verification/validation of machine resources (Rev5)

Name: Persistent Machine Verification and Validation for 20x
Requirement (Class C): Providers of FedRAMP 20x Class C offerings MUST verify and validate the status of machine-based information resources at least once every 3 days.
Gap: 20x-scoped rule; not applicable to the current Rev5 Class C certification
Required Change: Track under 20x readiness (workstream 09); no action for Rev5

Name: Non-Machine Verification and Validation
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST verify and validate the status of non-machine-based information resources at least once every 3 months.
Gap: No 3-month verification cadence for non-machine-based resources
Required Change: Verify/validate non-machine-based resources at least every 3 months (Class C)

Name: Persistently Complete Detection
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD persistently perform vulnerability detection on all information resources that are NOT likely to drift, at least once every month.
Gap: Monthly cadence likely meets this but full coverage of non-drift resources is unconfirmed
Required Change: Confirm non-drift resources are detected at least monthly with complete coverage (Class C)

Name: Persistent Drift Detection
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD persistently perform vulnerability detection on all information resources that are likely to drift, at least once every 14 days.
Gap: No drift-based detection cadence
Required Change: Detect on resources likely to drift at least every 14 days (Class C)

Name: Persistent Sample Detection
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD persistently perform vulnerability detection on representative samples of similar machine-based information resources, at least once every 3 days.
Gap: Cadence far short of the Class C 3-day requirement for representative samples
Required Change: Detect on representative samples of similar machine-based resources at least every 3 days

Name: Mitigation and Remediation Expectations
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD partially mitigate vulnerabilities, fully mitigate vulnerabilities, or remediate vulnerabilities to a lower Potential Agency Impact N-rating within the timeframes from evaluation shown below, factoring for the current Potential Agency Impact N-rating as defined in VER-EVA-EPA (Estimate Potential Agency Impact), internet reachability, and likely exploitability:
Gap: Remediation clock is CVSS-based from discovery, not PAIN/IRV/LEV from evaluation
Required Change: Implement the Class C PVR matrix (PAIN x IRV/LEV), clock from evaluation date; rebuild Jira SLA automation

Name: Remaining Vulnerabilities
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD mitigate or remediate remaining vulnerabilities during routine operations as determined necessary by the provider.
Gap: Remaining un-remediated vulns not tracked against the accepted-vuln threshold
Required Change: Track remaining vulnerabilities toward the 192-day accepted-vulnerability line

Name: Assume It's Automatable
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST assume the exploitation of vulnerabilities can be automated UNLESS they have evidence proving otherwise.
Current Process: DR/false-positive determinations assume a benign default
Gap: Determinations assert the safer state rather than proving it
Required Change: Default automatable=true; require evidence to claim not-automatable in the DR template

Name: Evaluation Factors
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD consider at least the following factors when considering the context of the cloud service offering to evaluate detected vulnerabilities:
Gap: Evaluation factor analysis is not captured in a structured way
Required Change: Capture the EFA factor checklist (Criticality, Reachability, Exploitability, Detectability, Prevalence, Privilege, Proximate Vulns, Known Threats)

Name: Evaluate False Positives
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD evaluate detected vulnerabilities, considering the context of the cloud service offering, to determine if they are false positive vulnerabilities.
Gap: FP determination does not carry IRV/LEV/PAIN context, so it can be internally inconsistent
Required Change: Move FP evaluation into the evaluation stage; require consistency with the IRV/LEV/PAIN analysis

Name: Evaluate Internet-Reachability
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST evaluate detected vulnerabilities, considering the context of the cloud service offering, to determine if they are internet-reachable vulnerabilities.
Gap: Internet-reachability is not formally evaluated or recorded per finding
Required Change: Add IRV enrichment from an asset-exposure map (external path, incl. behind proxy/LB/WAF); record IRV

Name: Evaluate Exploitability
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST evaluate detected vulnerabilities, considering the context of the cloud service offering, to determine if they are likely exploitable vulnerabilities.
Gap: Exploitability is not formally evaluated or recorded per finding
Required Change: Add LEV enrichment (KEV, exploit/weaponization signal, privilege/preconditions); record LEV

Name: Estimate Potential Agency Impact
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST evaluate detected vulnerabilities, considering the context of the cloud service offering, to estimate the potential agency impact of exploitation on government customers AND assign one of the following Potential Agency Impact N-ratings (PAIN):
Gap: No Potential Agency Impact (PAIN N1-N5) rating assigned
Required Change: Assign PAIN N1-N5 per finding via first-pass scoring plus human confirm

Name: Group Vulnerabilities
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD evaluate detected vulnerabilities, considering the context of the cloud service offering, to identify logical groupings of affected information resources that may improve the efficiency and effectiveness of vulnerability response by consolidating further activity; FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response rules are then applied to these consolidated groupings of vulnerabilities instead of each individual detected instance.
Current Process: One Jira issue per host per plugin
Gap: No grouping; volume is per-host-per-plugin
Required Change: Add a grouping key so one evaluation covers identical instances across sampled resources

Name: Accepted Vulnerability Info
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST include the following information on accepted vulnerabilities when reporting on vulnerability detection and response activity:
Gap: No separate reporting path for accepted vulnerabilities
Required Change: Add the accepted-vulnerability field set per the accepted-vulnerability-info JSON schema

Name: High-Level Overviews
Requirement (Class C): Providers SHOULD include high-level overviews of ALL vulnerability detection and response activities conducted during this period for the cloud service offering; this includes vulnerability disclosure programs, bug bounty programs, penetration testing, assessments, etc.
Gap: No high-level overview section in reporting
Required Change: Add a high-level overview to the human-readable monthly report

Name: Responsible Disclosure
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST NOT irresponsibly disclose specific sensitive information about vulnerabilities that would likely lead to exploitation, but MUST disclose sufficient information for informed risk-based decision-making to all necessary parties.
Current Process: Reports not screened for sensitive disclosure
Gap: Report content is not screened against irresponsible disclosure of exploit detail
Required Change: Add a screening step so reports do not irresponsibly disclose sensitive vulnerability detail

Name: Persistent Reporting
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST report vulnerability detection and response activity (including persistent verification and validation) to all necessary parties persistently, summarizing ALL activity since the previous report; these reports are FedRAMP Certification Data and are subject to FedRAMP Certification Data Sharing rules.
Gap: Reports are point-in-time counts, not persistent lifecycle summaries, and not treated as Certification Data
Required Change: Produce a persistent report summarizing all activity since the prior report; treat as Certification Data

Name: Responsible Public Disclosure
Requirement (Class C): Providers MAY responsibly disclose vulnerabilities publicly or with other parties if the provider determines doing so will NOT likely lead to exploitation.
Gap: No defined responsible public-disclosure handling
Required Change: Optional: define if/how responsible public disclosure is handled

Name: Vulnerability Details
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST include the following information (if applicable) on detected vulnerabilities when reporting on vulnerability detection and response activity, UNLESS it is an accepted vulnerability:
Gap: Records lack the required VDT fields (detection time/source, eval-complete, IRV, LEV, PAIN history, next reduction, overdue, disposition)
Required Change: Add the VDT field set to Jira and export to the vulnerability-detail JSON schema

Name: Evaluate Vulnerabilities Quickly
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD evaluate ALL vulnerabilities as required by VER-EVA (Evaluation) within 5 days of detection.
Gap: No 5-day evaluation timer from detection
Required Change: Add a 5-day evaluation SLA from detection (Class C) with overdue logic

Name: Internet-Reachable Incidents
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD treat internet-reachable likely exploitable vulnerabilities where Potential Agency Impact N-rating > 3 as a FedRAMP Reportable Incident until they are partially mitigated vulnerabilities at N3 or below.
Gap: No auto-promotion of high-impact reachable findings to incidents
Required Change: Auto-flag N4/N5 internet-reachable + likely-exploitable as candidate Reportable Incident (Class C SHOULD) into the Sentinel-to-Jira path

Name: Mark Accepted Vulnerabilities
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST categorize any vulnerability that is not or will not be fully mitigated or remediated within 192 days of evaluation as an accepted vulnerability.
Gap: No categorization of vulns past the accepted-vulnerability threshold
Required Change: Auto-categorize vulns not fully mitigated within 192 days of evaluation as accepted

Name: Monthly Activity Report
Requirement (Class C): Providers MUST report vulnerability detection and response activity to all necessary parties in a consistent format that is human readable at least monthly.
Gap: Summary is counts, not a full evaluate/mitigate lifecycle report
Required Change: Produce a human-readable activity report at least monthly covering the full lifecycle

Name: Historical Activity
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications SHOULD make all recent historical vulnerability detection and response activity available in JSON format for automated retrieval by all necessary parties (e.g. using an API service or similar); this information SHOULD be updated persistently, at least once every 14 days.
Gap: No machine-readable historical activity feed
Required Change: Produce historical VER activity per the historical-ver-activity JSON schema

Name: Non-Internet-Reachable Incidents
Requirement (Class C): Providers with Class C Certifications MAY treat likely exploitable vulnerabilities that are NOT internet-reachable where Potential Agency Impact N-rating = 5 as a FedRAMP Reportable Incident until they are partially mitigated vulnerabilities at N4 or below.
Gap: No handling of high-impact non-reachable findings as possible incidents
Required Change: Optional (Class C MAY): flag N5 non-reachable + likely-exploitable for incident consideration

Name: Consider Security Category
Requirement (Class C): Agencies SHOULD consider the Security Category noted in their Authorization to Operate of the federal information system that includes the cloud service offering in its boundary and assign appropriate information security resources for reviewing Ongoing Certification Reports, attending Quarterly Reviews, and other ongoing FedRAMP Certification Data.

Name: Review Ongoing Reports
Requirement (Class C): Agencies MUST review each Ongoing Certification Report to understand how changes to the cloud service offering may impact the previously agreed-upon risk tolerance documented in the agency's Authorization to Operate of a federal information system that includes the cloud service offering in its boundary.

Name: Ongoing Review
Requirement (Class C): FedRAMP MUST periodically review FedRAMP Incident Evaluation and Communication implementation with providers based on lack of reporting or other information.

Name: Maintain Agency Plans of Action and Milestones
Requirement (Class C): Agencies SHOULD use vulnerability information reported by the Provider to maintain Plans of Action and Milestones for agency security programs when relevant according to agency security policies (such as if the agency takes action to mitigate the risk of exploitation or authorized the continued use of a cloud service with accepted vulnerabilities that put agency information systems at risk).

Name: Review Vulnerability Reports
Requirement (Class C): Agencies SHOULD review the information provided in vulnerability reports at appropriate and reasonable intervals commensurate with the expectations and risk posture indicated by their Authorization to Operate, and SHOULD use automated processing and filtering of machine readable information from cloud service providers.

Name: Sensitive Details
Requirement (Class C): FedRAMP MAY require providers to share additional information or details about vulnerabilities, including sensitive information that would likely lead to exploitation, as part of review, response or investigation by necessary parties.

Name: Additional Requirements
Requirement (Class C): FedRAMP MAY require providers to share additional vulnerability information, alternative reports, or to report at an alternative frequency as a condition of a FedRAMP Corrective Action Plan or other agreements with federal agencies.
